From: Amelia Tran <amelia.tran@edgecorp.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-25T08:41:00Z
Subject: Spike in p99 & 5xx across Hosted API - urgent

Jonas,

We started seeing sustained p99 latency spikes and a small but growing fraction of 5xx errors on our calls to the Hosted API starting late last night (2026-03-24 22:30 PST). Throughput also dropped ~18% on average for our steady-state traffic. Attached are a reduced set of request traces and the service logs we pulled from our side (edgecorp_logs_0325.zip).

Initial observations from our ops team: several replicas reported OOMs or GPU allocation failures, and the traces show long tail token times (p95->p99 regressions). Can Redwood confirm whether there were any infra/runtime deploys or model rollouts during this window? This is impacting our availability SLA — we need a mitigation plan and an ETA.

We'd like an urgent call with SRE/engineering in the next 90 minutes and visibility into any short-term workarounds. Our account team copy is dataops@edgecorp.com.

Thanks,
Amelia Tran
Head of ML Ops, EdgeCorp

On Wed, Mar 25, 2026 at 08:41AM Amelia Tran <amelia.tran@edgecorp.com> wrote:
> Jonas,
>
> We started seeing sustained p99 latency spikes...

Thanks for the heads up and logs, Amelia. Quick triage summary from SRE: we see repeated GPU allocation failures and OOM events on several nodes serving the Hosted API around the same timeframe. Behind the scenes, the runtime is reporting many small allocations and several large KV cache allocations for EdgeCorp’s traffic pattern. The pattern is consistent with memory fragmentation causing occasional allocation failures which manifest as high tail latency and 5xxs.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (low risk):
- Trim per-session KV caches aggressively for EdgeCorp’s route for the next 6 hours (reduces memory pressure)
- Reduce batch size for their route from 48->24 to reduce peak per-inference allocation
- Optionally move EdgeCorp traffic to our Dedicated pool (requires a short routing change, ETA ~10m)

We have a runbook snippet attached with the exact commands (runbook-kv-cache-trim.txt). I recommend we apply the KV-trim + batch-size reduction now and observe; if errors persist, start routing to Dedicated.

Grace
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: runbook-kv-cache-trim.txt]
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-25T11:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Spike in p99 & 5xx across Hosted API - urgent

Adding runtime context from the engine team. Observations from heap dumps and trace logs:
- We see fragmentation on the GPU allocator: frequent small allocations followed by large contiguous KV allocations that fail when fragmentation is high.
- A kernel-level change deployed last week (memory allocator heuristic tweak) increased allocation locality for some models but appears to interact badly with this workload’s allocation size distribution.

Hypothesis: the allocator heuristic is causing less defragmentation under certain allocation patterns, leading to transient OOMs and p99 spikes.

Recommended actions (engineering):
1) Immediate: apply the SRE mitigations (kv-trim + reduce batch) to buy time.
2) Short term (canary within 2 hours): rollback allocator heuristic to previous version on a small percentage of nodes to validate regressions. Rolling back is low-risk and reversible; if that restores headroom, we can widen the rollback.
3) Medium term: implement an opportunistic defragmentation pass in the allocator (tracked as runtime-allocator#334).

I’ll prepare a canary rollout PR and coordinate with SRE for a window. If we proceed, we need approval to shift ~10% of EdgeCorp traffic to the rollback nodes for 30–60m.

—Marcus Lin
Software Engineer, Runtime

Amelia — following our triage and the runbook steps, here’s the condensed plan and timeline: 

Actions taken (T+1h):
- Applied KV-cache trimming for EdgeCorp’s route (started 2026-03-25T11:20Z)
- Reduced batch size for the route to 24 (started 2026-03-25T11:40Z)
- Monitoring shows immediate reduction in 5xxs and lower p95; p99 improved but some residual spikes remain.

Planned next steps (T+2–4h):
- Launch a targeted canary rollback of the allocator heuristic on 10% of nodes (Marcus will coordinate).
- If canary shows improvement, widen rollback to 50% within 4–6h and then full rollback by EOD if safe.

Compensation and exec touch: we understand this impacted your SLA. I’ve looped in Marissa (Product) and Stephanie (Head of Customer Success) to discuss a service credit and a post-incident executive readout. We’ll confirm credits after we finish the RCA.

Call-to-action: Amelia — please confirm whether routing to Dedicated for a short window is acceptable as an immediate fallback (we can do this now and switch back when stable). Also flag any constraints on maintenance windows.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll keep updates frequent.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
